- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots; cap next 3–5 days’ forecast at +5% below peak.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) and price is falling, model underestimates drop; add 2–5% downward bias to forecast.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon; apply 3–5% downward adjustment to first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated small positive signals (e.g., 0.20), model overreacts; dampen forecast volatility by 10–20%.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid extrapolating recent momentum; use 3–5 day moving average as baseline for correction.
